evals.prompt: You are working in the plain project at <fixture-repo>. It has a README but no AGENTS.md. Initialize it with the agent-setup skill using the Standard profile. The owner uses one implementation workflow, does not separate planning, review, or integration into stages, expects no concurrent workers, and requires explicit user assignment. Use the build, test, lint, and format commands documented in the fixture README. Work only in the fixture; do not call the network or change repository settings.
evals.expected_output: A Standard-profile agent setup whose discovery accounts for optional stage separation but whose AGENTS.md has no work-unit stage record, treating the absent record as the normal single implementation workflow.
expectations: The setup applies the Standard profile and produces the normal managed sections and project-specific checks
The response shows that stage separation was considered during discovery
AGENTS.md contains no work-unit stage record or placeholder for one
The absence of a stage record is treated as the default single implementation workflow, not as drift or a missing section
Planning is not introduced or made mandatory

evals.prompt: You are working in the project at <fixture-repo>. Initialize it with the agent-setup skill using the Standard profile. The owner plans each assigned issue in one agent session and hands the issue to a fresh implementation session. Planning may edit only the issue contract and its plan comment; implementation may edit the repository only after a new explicit user assignment. Record these as project-specific stages with durable handoff state. Use the commands documented in the fixture README. Work only in the fixture; do not call the network or change repository settings.
evals.expected_output: An AGENTS.md with an unmanaged planning-to-implementation stage record. Both stages define activation, allowed mutations, required input, durable output, finish line, and transition; the issue and plan comment carry the handoff, and plan completion does not authorize implementation.
expectations: AGENTS.md records separate planning and implementation stages in unmanaged project-specific content
Both stages define activation, allowed mutations, required input, durable output, finish line, and transition
The planning stage may mutate only the issue contract and plan comment
The planning stage skips implementation-only session checklist steps such as updating the default branch, creating a branch, committing, pushing, and opening a PR
The issue and its plan comment, rather than chat context, carry the planning output into implementation
Completing the plan transitions the issue to a handoff state but does not authorize implementation
Implementation activation still requires a new explicit user assignment

evals.prompt: You are updating the existing agent-ready project at <fixture-repo>. Its AGENTS.md already has managed canonical blocks, an unmanaged planning and implementation stage record, and a complete four-field coordination model record. Use the agent-setup skill in update mode. Preserve the coordination record, the existing two stage definitions, and all other unmanaged content; refresh any canonical drift and add owner-requested review and integration stages. Review may change the branch only to address accepted findings; integration validates the current base and hands off an open green PR for a human merge. Work only in the fixture; do not call the network or change repository settings.
evals.expected_output: An updated AGENTS.md whose managed blocks match the canonical source, whose coordination model remains verbatim, and whose unmanaged stage record preserves planning and implementation while adding complete review and integration definitions. The new stages do not weaken explicit activation, human merge, or review gates.
expectations: The existing four-field coordination model record remains verbatim in unmanaged content
Existing planning and implementation stage definitions are preserved verbatim
Review and integration are added only because the owner explicitly requested them
Update mode treats only the requested stage-record additions as an exception to its untouched-unmanaged-content rule
All four stages define activation, allowed mutations, required input, durable output, finish line, and transition
The implementation stage stops at its recorded transition without starting separately declared review or integration actions
The stage record remains outside every managed block and other unmanaged content is preserved verbatim
Managed sections match the current canonical source after the update
Review mutations are limited to accepted findings, and integration ends at an open green PR for human merge

evals.expected_output: An updated AGENTS.md that adds the first owner-requested planning-only stage record outside managed blocks while preserving every pre-existing unmanaged instruction and leaving undeclared implementation under the default workflow and explicit activation rule.
expectations: Update mode creates a stage record because the owner explicitly requested first-time stage adoption
The new record contains only the planning stage with all six required fields
Planning mutations are limited to the issue contract and plan comment
Undeclared implementation retains the default workflow and still requires a new explicit user assignment
All pre-existing unmanaged project guidance remains verbatim

AGENTS.md contains no coordination model record or placeholder for one
The absent record is treated as serial work, not missing content

evals.prompt: You are initializing the project at <fixture-repo> with the agent-setup skill using the Standard profile. Its only coordination source is a draft PLAN.md that sketches API and UI lanes, a dependency graph, and three parallel workers; no code or work-unit history corroborates those ideas, and review capacity is unknown. The owner explicitly wants a compact coordination record that captures today's justified model and when to revisit it. Work only in the fixture; do not call the network or change repository settings.
evals.expected_output: An unmanaged fixed-field coordination record that treats the draft plan as uncorroborated evidence, keeps the project on a serial baseline, states unknown review capacity, and names observable reassessment triggers without adopting the proposed lanes or graph.
expectations: The plan is described as evidence rather than authoritative project policy
The selected current shape remains the safe serial baseline because no code or history corroborates the plan
The record contains current shape, evidence basis, detailed mechanics, and reassessment trigger fields outside managed blocks
The proposed API and UI lanes, dependency graph, and three-worker width are not adopted
The reassessment trigger names observable corroboration such as implemented boundaries, repeated work-unit history, or confirmed review capacity

evals.prompt: You are adopting agent-setup management in the mature project at <fixture-repo>. Its existing AGENTS.md has useful project guidance but no managed markers or coordination record. Its code, architecture notes, and work-unit history show one maintainer completing small serial changes with no recurring independent streams, shared-contract bottleneck, intentional stacks, or parallel review capacity. Adopt the Standard profile, preserve the existing guidance, and run coordination discovery. The owner has not requested a coordination record. Work only in the fixture; do not call the network or change repository settings.
evals.expected_output: An adopted Standard-profile setup that preserves existing guidance, considers the mature repository's evidence, keeps its proven simple serial behavior, and does not force a coordination record or richer topology.
expectations: Adoption runs project-specific coordination discovery before completing the managed-block comparison
Existing unmarked project guidance is preserved through adoption
The setup inspects code, architecture notes, work-unit history, and owner capacity rather than equating repository age with complexity
The selected coordination shape remains the safe serial baseline
AGENTS.md contains no coordination model record because the owner did not request one and richer coordination is unsupported
No named streams, typed relation vocabulary, integration spine, or claim mechanism is introduced
Existing simple project behavior remains intact

evals.prompt: You are initializing the project at <fixture-repo> with the agent-setup skill using the Standard profile. Its architecture documentation and six completed work-unit records show two recurring, stable, independently reviewable streams that repeatedly use the same boundaries; the owner confirms those boundaries remain useful. Record the justified coordination model, keep long mechanics in project documentation, and do not infer any stream from directory names alone. evals.expected_output: An unmanaged stable-named-streams coordination record with evidence from recurring history, a maximum width of two, a pointer to project-owned mechanics, and reassessment triggers; the detailed document keeps individual work contracts authoritative.
expectations: Named streams are justified by recurring work-unit history plus owner confirmation, not by directory names
The coordination record contains all four fixed fields outside managed blocks
The current shape names stable work streams and caps concurrent active units at two
Detailed stream boundaries and interactions live in project documentation referenced from AGENTS.md
Individual work contracts remain authoritative and claims, if any, remain occupancy signals only
Reassessment triggers cover boundaries becoming unstable or review and integration capacity changing

evals.prompt: You are initializing the project at <fixture-repo> with the agent-setup skill using the High-assurance profile. The owner requires decision notes for shared-schema changes, coordination-policy changes, and destructive migrations. Existing code, architecture documentation, and work-unit history show independent component work converging through one shared schema: schema changes must serialize, one integration role orders convergence, and prior units separately used start order, merge order, intentional stacking, and mutual exclusion. The owner confirms one integrator can handle two independent component units at once. Record the justified model and its detailed mechanics without treating schema serialization as component ownership. Work only in the fixture; do not call the network or change repository settings.
evals.expected_output: A High-assurance setup with the supplied mandatory-note classes and an unmanaged integration-spine coordination record capped at two independent component units, with detailed project documentation that separates shared-schema serialization from component ownership and defines start, merge, stacking, and exclusion relations distinctly.
expectations: AGENTS.md records the High-assurance profile and the supplied shared-schema, coordination-policy, and destructive-migration mandatory-note classes
The current shape is an integration spine or serialized shared-contract domain supported by code, architecture, history, and owner evidence
The coordination record contains all four fixed fields outside managed blocks and points to detailed project mechanics
Shared-schema serialization is modeled separately from component ownership
Start order, merge order, intentional stacking, and mutual exclusion have distinct operational meanings
Unknown or materially ambiguous relations serialize until the designated authority resolves them
The recommended concurrency width is capped at two independent component units by actual integration capacity
